summary: Full-stack testing of Delhi Sultanate Court app: 16 backend pytest cases (auth, trial/turn LLM proxy, balance formula, evidence system, save/load, complete+stats) — all 16 PASSED after correcting one test bug (email lowercased server-side). Frontend Playwright covers Auth -> Cover -> Rules -> ChooseSultan -> Cinematic -> Trial -> Speak -> LLM turn -> Options/Evidence modals -> Continue Trial resume. All critical flows PASSED. Balance formula verified (waytooasy good×5.0/bad×0.2, medium 1.0/1.0, impossible 0.2/5.0). Evidence gating on even rounds confirmed. Exploit-proof presentation confirmed (works only with granted evidence + present keyword). Auto-save + Continue Trial resumes at correct round.

issues: Escape key does not close the evidence modal; only the CLOSE button works. Minor UX polish — consider adding onKeyDown handler.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~475 lines; still manageable but approaching split threshold — auth, LLM, trial, save/stats routes could be moved into modules under /app/backend/routers/ for future growth.

sultan_speech LLM call is awaited sequentially AFTER the 3-way asyncio.gather; consider adding it to the gather when it does not depend on the JSON mood (currently it does, so ordering is correct — acceptable).
compute_suspicion multipliers are correct verbatim ports; goodWeight=farukhMult/qaziMult, badWeight=qaziMult/farukhMult confirmed against test cases.
Frontend evidence modal lacks Escape-to-close; minor.
seed_data_creation: No new seed. Created ephemeral TEST_ users during register test and a completed match record in stats test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_court_backend.py — a single pytest file with 6 classes covering all endpoints. Uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL env var. Trial-turn tests hit real Claude (10-25s each). Save/Load test cleans its own state. Frontend testids all present per review request; testable via Playwright without issue.
rca of the issue: N/A — no defects found. First iteration is solid.
